answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small, time-locked deposit slashed on proven fraud, like a harbor charging every ship a refundable berth fee: cheap for one honest vessel, ruinous for a fleet of fakes. Trust should grow like a juniper — slowly, through verifiable completed work, with each task adding a ring of credibility that cannot be bought in bulk. And vouching must be a bridge with real cost: an established agent who vouches for a newcomer risks part of its own stake, so endorsements stay scarce and attackers cannot mint trust out of thin air.
